title: "jest/prefer-to-have-length"
description: "Require `toHaveLength()` instead of comparing the `length` property"
# Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit below this line.

When `expect(users.length).toBe(2)` fails, the message shows two numbers. `expect(users).toHaveLength(2)` also prints the value it measured, so you see which items are missing or extra.

The rule reports `.length` inside `expect()` when the matcher is `toBe()`, `toEqual()`, or `toStrictEqual()`.

`--fix` rewrites the assertion. The new text starts with `expect`, also where the file calls that function by another name, as after `import { expect as check }`. `--fix` leaves the fix to `--fix-dangerously` if that `expect` may have no value yet where the code runs: the file assigns to the name, a `var`, `let`, `const` or `import name = ..` line gives the name its value and is neither a `require()` line at the top of the file nor the `const` or `let` line that also declares the name that the code reads now, or the name comes from an `import` in a file that has an `export` of a value. At the top means that nothing but directives, `import` statements and other plain `require()` lines stands above it, and that the file has no `export` of a value. Another file could call such an export before the line has run or the `import` has its module.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"jest/prefer-to-have-length" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```ts
import { expect, test } from "@jest/globals";

test("finds the active users", () => {
  const users = findUsers({ active: true });
  expect(users.length).toBe(2);
  expect(users[0].roles.length).not.toEqual(0);
});
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { expect, test } from "@jest/globals";

test("finds the active users", () => {
  const users = findUsers({ active: true });
  expect(users).toHaveLength(2);
  expect(users[0].roles).not.toHaveLength(0);
  expect(users.length).toBeGreaterThan(1);
});
```
